start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:keep-a-link-in-bio-page with store {\"where\": \"postgresql database example_shop on my own computer\", \"language\": \"SQL (PostgreSQL)\", \"credential_name\": \"example-shop-postgres-connection\"} and changes [{\"on\": true, \"title\": \"Example shop\", \"links\": [{\"link_id\": \"shop\", \"label\": \"Shop\", \"url\": \"https://example.com/shop\"}]}]."
no_lists_because: It names no list: the page and its counts are kept in the person's own store, in whatever form that store keeps things, and store says where and in which language.
instructions: 1. Keep the store's login in your vault under a name you choose, and say where the store is and how it is spoken to.
2. Say "Run workflow:keep-a-link-in-bio-page" with store, and the changes, visits and opens to keep.
3. The first run makes the store's own objects once and proves them on the example attempts: every attempt must give the outcome the intent says, or the run stops and says which.

4. Every later run keeps the changes and counts through those objects; a visit to a page that is off, or an open of a link the page does not list, is refused with the store's own words, and turning the page back on keeps its code.

worked_examples.title: The page turned on, with one link, then a visit from Instagram counted
worked_examples.ask: Turn my link page on with my shop link, and count a visit from Instagram.

store.where: postgresql database example_shop on my own computer

worked_examples.given: The look step found the page kept in the tables link_page, link_page_counts and link_page_totals, made by an earlier run.
worked_examples.hands_back: kept_ids ["shop"], refused [] and found_ids ["shop"]; the page reads on with its code, and the visit reads once under instagram.
